title: Black Friday 2025 — Regional Model Failover and Emergency Model-Swap Retrospective
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary:
This retrospective summarizes the November 27, 2025 Black Friday incident in which a cascading regional capacity degradation in us-west-2 coincided with an emergency model-swap that caused elevated tail latency and a ~41% drop in successful hosted generation requests for ~112 minutes. The actions taken kept customer-facing downtime under 1.5 hours at the global level, but exposed operational gaps in our model-swap fencing, circuit-breaker defaults, and synthetic canary sensitivity thresholds.

Scope and impact:
- Affected surface: Redwood Hosted API (text generation endpoints) and a subset of Dedicated tenants using us-west-2 regional pools.
- User-visible incidents: increased 5xx rates and token timeouts for 6% of active tenants in the window; highest impact to tenants with latency SLOs <= 200ms.
- Quantitative metrics (peak):
  - 5xx rate (us-west-2 region): 3.8% (baseline 0.05%)
  - Median generation latency (global): +270ms vs baseline
  - Tail (99.9th) latency spikes in affected region: from 2.1s to 9.6s
  - Extra tokens billed (failed retries & fallbacks): ~1.9M tokens (~$650 net cost)
content_2:
Timeline (UTC):
1) 2025-11-27 14:02 — Synthetic canary for model-variant /redwood-002 failed health check in us-west-2; on-call SRE notified via pager. Canary mismatch: the canary synthetic used a short prompt set (~12 tokens) not representative of tenant median length (140 tokens).
2) 2025-11-27 14:10 — Operator triggered emergency model-swap to the CPU-quantized fallback across affected pool; rollout used the standard rollout DSL with 10% initial traffic.
3) 14:11–14:28 — Unexpected KV-cache warming pattern + aggressive autoscaler thrash led to extended request queuing; the 10% model-variant had a higher CPU path for large-sequence workloads which increased per-request service time.
4) 14:30 — Automated routing fallback attempted to route excess traffic to other regions; regional capacity was soft-capped by quota manager and rejected bursts leading to retries and tokenized backpressure.
5) 15:40 — On-call enacted manual prioritized-tenant steering and increased canary threshold; traffic normalized by 16:54 after staged rollback and progressive cache rehydration.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Primary cause: Model-variant selection during emergency swap introduced a runtime path that deoptimized for long-sequence requests (KV-cache miss amplification + slower kernel path). This path was not exercised by our short synthetic canaries.
- Secondary causes:
  - Canary design mismatch: synthetic prompts not representative of production length distribution.
  - Rollout safety parameters: default 10% fanout allowed the slower path to amplify queuing when autoscaler thrash occurred. No per-variant CPU headroom check executed prior to swap.
  - Quota & burst caps in adjacent regions prevented clean cross-region shedding; fallback retries amplified load.

Detection and mitigation (what we did):
1) Immediate containment: temporarily freeze auto-rollout for model-variants and engage manual routing lock to limit swap fanout to 0%. Owner: Runtime Ops (Alex Huang).
2) Prioritized tenant steering: applied tenant-level sticky routing to known enterprise customers to minimize exposure. Owner: Customer Reliability (Nina Patel).
3) Rolling rollback: reverted to the previous model-variant incrementally, with additional warmup requests generated by the operator to rehydrate prefix and KV caches. Owner: Serving Runtime Team (Tobias Reed).
4) Cost containment: applied short-term token caps on automated retry logic to limit billing blowout. Owner: Billing Ops (Samir Gupta).

Why the mitigations initially underperformed:
- Cache rehydration was manual and slow because our automated prefix rehydration service uses TTL windows that assume standard rollouts (not emergency swaps).
- The autoscaler thrash was caused by request latency feedback loops to the CPU scheduler; we lacked a short-circuit that recognized model-variant CPU path elevation.

Action items (owner + ETA + verification):
1) Canary redesign: expand synthetic canary corpus to include representative length and token distribution (short, median, long).
   - Owner: QA & Evals (Priya Nair)
   - ETA: 2026-02-12
   - Verification: Canary pass/fail correlated with a 14-day rolling sample of production traffic.
2) Variant preflight CPU headroom check: enforce a pre-swap probe that runs a standardized 128/512/1024 token microbenchmark against the candidate model-variant and asserts latency and CPU utilization bounds.
   - Owner: Serving Runtime (Tobias Reed)
   - ETA: 2026-03-01
   - Verification: All scheduled swaps require probe success; probes logged centrally.
3) Rollout safety tightening: change emergency-swap default fanout to 2% with dependent auto-escalation only after headroom validation.
   - Owner: Platform Orchestration (Carla Mendes)
   - ETA: 2026-01-31
   - Verification: New default applied in staging and validated during next canary.
4) Automated progressive KV-prefix rehydration: implement a background operator that issues warmup requests following a geometric distribution across shard key prefixes to restore effective cache hit ratio within 10–20 minutes.
   - Owner: Cache & Runtime (Alex Huang)
   - ETA: 2026-04-15
   - Verification: Hit ratio and tail latency return-to-baseline within target window in staging failure simulations.
5) Cross-region burst policy refinement: add a soft-burst escrow that allows temporary spillover for up to 2 minutes with cost caps and backpressure signals propagated to origin.
   - Owner: SRE Capacity (Diego Martinez)
   - ETA: 2026-02-28
   - Verification: Fault injection test with synthetic regional failure.
6) Incident automation cookbook: create an operator-runbook snippet that performs a rapid model-swap abort and a safe-rollforward path with metrics checklist and CLI commands.
   - Owner: Oncall Documentation (Maya Thompson)
   - ETA: 2026-01-31
   - Verification: Playbook exercised in next game day.

Runbook snippet (CLI examples and safe checklist):
1) Abort rollout: redwoodctl rollout abort --variant <variant-id> --region us-west-2
2) Lock routing: redwoodctl routing lock --region us-west-2 --reason "emergency-model-path"
3) Issue progressive rehydration wave (operator): redwoodctl cache warmup --variant <variant-id> --wave 0.05 --sequences "128,512,1024"
4) Checklist before re-enable:
   - Confirm preflight probe success (3/3 sizes)
   - Verify KV hit ratio improved >= 70% vs pre-incident baseline
   - Validate region-level CPU headroom >= 18% for the variant
   - Confirm cross-region spill escrow available

Operational changes (policy and automation):
- New policy: Emergency model-swap must pass automatic preflight or be restricted to a 2% fanout and an operator-confirmed warmup plan.
- New automation: Canary corpus expansion + automatic variant preflight job + progressive KV rehydration operator + regional spill escrow.

Lessons learned and recommendations:
- Synthetic canaries must mirror production token length distributions; short prompt canaries provide false confidence for long-sequence workloads.
- Emergency rollouts are high-risk; instrument preflight checks that exercise multiple resource dimensions (CPU, memory, KV cache behavior).
- Fallback logic must consider cross-region quota and provide cost-aware short-term spill allowances to prevent retry storms.
- Invest in automated prefix rehydration to reduce manual toil and shorten recovery windows.

Appendix A — Incident timeline table (key events):
| Time (UTC) | Event | Immediate effect | Owner/action |
|------------|-------|------------------|--------------|
| 14:02 | Canary fail detected | Pager fired | QA/Evals review |
| 14:10 | Emergency model-swap initiated (10% fanout) | Small increase in median latency | Runtime Ops |
| 14:15 | Autoscaler thrash observed | Queueing and longer tails | SRE intervene |
| 15:40 | Manual tiered steering & rollback begin | Traffic stabilization begins | Serving Runtime |
| 16:54 | Service normalized | Post-incident checks start | Cross-team handoff |

Appendix B — Verification scenarios added to the resilience lab:
- Scenario 1: Emergency-swap with long-sequence workload (1–2M requests simulated) — verify progressive rehydration achieves 75% hit ratio within 20 minutes.
- Scenario 2: Cross-region spill under quota saturation — verify spill escrow allows controlled traffic absorption without retries.
- Scenario 3: Autoscaler thrash with variant CPU path elevation — verify short-circuit local-shed prevents tail amplification.

Owners for remediation (compact):
- Canary redesign: Priya Nair (QA & Evals)
- Preflight CPU probe: Tobias Reed (Serving Runtime)
- Rollout defaults: Carla Mendes (Platform Orchestration)
- KV rehydration operator: Alex Huang (Cache & Runtime)
- Cross-region escrow: Diego Martinez (SRE Capacity)
- Playbook and docs: Maya Thompson (Oncall Documentation)

Follow-up review: scheduled cross-team tabletop and game-day for 2026-02-18 to validate the automation and runbook changes.

End of retrospective. For questions or objections to action assignments, ping the owner_team channel: #platform-ops-retrospectives.
